title: Research: seed 5 exact joint-boundary census for PR589 r659 (no kappa)
body:
## Result

Adds a scoped negative-result audit for seed 5: the exact jointly boundary-adaptive frame census for PR589 A[2071] and B[820] at shared register 659. Out of 20 dynamically generated frame assignments, 12 pass both reciprocal boundary checks and complete touched-register chains; the remaining 8 fail the restored A upper boundary. The legal assignments yield 8 paid-profile ties and 4 strict losses, with no improvement or unresolved comparison. The fixed-original-boundary control also yields the same 12 legal pairs, so this cut exposes no joint-only choice.

All 12 legal assignments replay through `wlib.rebuild_C` and `wlib.paid`. The baseline profile, relaxed-boundary rejection, exact rational loss witnesses, frame domains and source pins are recorded in the package. This does not claim a stronger bound or a new kappa.

## Reproduce

Base commit: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`.

```sh
python3 research/bit589-boundary-adaptive-r659-seed05/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_BIT589_BOUNDARY_ADAPTIVE_R659 seed=5 candidates=20 valid=12 joint_only=0`.

The package metadata/source pin check passes. Local direct verification ran on CPython 3.14.7; the registered replay requires Python 3.12, which is unavailable locally, so its hosted check is the remaining interpreter-specific verification.

## Scope and credit

This tests one seed-selected operation pair on the pinned PR589 word. It does not cover other registers, larger move sets, other words, or recursive constructions. The accepted #1094 selected result and its assumptions are unchanged; the assembly is still complex-limited.

The task selection records three candidates and the OS-random seed. This work extends the fixed-option census/open question in #1382 using the exact transport and pricing methods of #1345. Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. New package material is Apache-2.0.
